question: I welcome the European Commission’s interest in reducing resource consumption in the digital sector. However, the current proposal contains major hidden economic traps for Central and Eastern European countries.

I see a number of serious weaknesses: an absurdly low threshold (500 kW), which directly hits the servers of local SMEs through disproportionate bureaucracy and audit costs, rather than targeting IT giants; the fanciful requirement of waste heat recovery, which is unworkable in our district heating networks without colossal investments, giving an unfair advantage to Western Europe; the forced tripling of data capacities without funding for electricity grids, which risks passing modernisation costs directly onto household bills.
In view of the above, can the Commission clarify the following? 1.
Why has it set such a low threshold (500 kW), stifling local IT providers in countries such as Romania, instead of only targeting large hyperscalers?
How will it ensure that labelling does not discriminate against investments from the East, given the massive discrepancies between district heating networks in the EU when it comes to waste heat?

What specific financial support will it allocate to energy transmission and distribution operators to ensure that it is not the citizens who pay the cost of adapting networks to data centre consumption?
